hero.badge: A learning system, not a notebook
hero.text: Studytracker is a system that grows, reinforces and strengthens what you learn. Collect materials, turn them into questions and flashcards, write essays and get them checked, defend your knowledge and see exactly where it still cracks.

loop.title: One loop. Three verbs.
loop.text: Notes alone fade. Studytracker keeps knowledge moving through a loop that grows it, reinforces it and makes it stronger every time you come back.

grow.text: Give everything you learn a place to live: an article, a lecture, a set of new words. Your knowledge base starts here.

reinforce.text: Turn it into questions and flashcards. Pulling an answer out of memory makes it stronger than reading it again.

strengthen.text: Defend what you know, get an honest score and see which topics crack. Then go back and grow exactly those.

loop.footer: Weak spots from Strengthen become the next things you Grow. The loop never stops, and neither does your progress.

how.title: From the first note to knowledge that holds
how.text: Five steps, one material. Click through them, the demos are live.

material.label: Add a material
material.title: Everything starts with a material
material.text: An article, a video, a practice task or a test. Give it a status and a subject, then attach notes, questions and a dictionary to it.

questions.label: Create questions
questions.title: Turn it into questions
questions.text: Write questions in your own words or let AI draft them, and pick a difficulty. Three types cover most of what you need to check:

defend.label: Self defending
defend.title: Defend what you know
defend.text: Self defending is a quiz over a material's questions. They come in random order, and with every answer you say how sure you are. Try it:

score.label: Get a score
score.title: A score that is honest
score.text: Every answer gets 0 to 100. Open answers are checked by exact match first, then by fuzzy match, so a typo does not cost you; close answers in other words are checked by meaning. The attempt score is a weighted average where hard questions count three times.

statistics.label: Watch it grow
statistics.title: See what is getting stronger
statistics.text: Statistics follow you over time: score trend, study streak, accuracy by difficulty, how well your confidence matches reality and which subjects are your weakest.

lines: 📚 Knowledge is the only backpack that gets lighter the more you fill it.
🧠 Your brain called. It wants a snack: one small material, please.
🌱 Every expert was once a beginner who didn't quit after the first page.
☕ Coffee in one hand, curiosity in the other. Perfect setup.
🐢 Slow progress is still progress. Turtles finish races too.
🎯 Ten focused minutes beat an hour of “I'll start in a second”.
🔥 The best time to start was yesterday. The second best is right now.
🦉 Night owl or early bird, this page is open for both.
🧩 Today's confusion is tomorrow's “oh, that's easy”.
🚀 Small daily steps quietly turn into giant leaps.
🍕 Learning is like pizza: even a single slice counts.
🌧️ Bad day? Learn one tiny thing. It's a win nobody can take away.
💡 Questions are just answers that haven't been met yet.
🏋️ Memory is a muscle. Today is leg day for your neurons.
🎧 Put on a good playlist and pick one material. Future you says thanks.
🐝 Busy bees make honey; curious minds make knowledge.
📈 You don't have to be great to start, but you have to start to be great.
🌍 Every word you learn is a new window to look out of.
🧘 Breathe in, open a material, breathe out. You've got this.
🕯️ A candle loses nothing by lighting another one. Neither does sharing what you learn.
🐣 Everything you love doing now, you once didn't know how to do.
🧭 Lost in a topic? That's just exploring with extra steps.
🎲 Spin the wheel of knowledge: today's prize is whatever you open next.
🌙 Tired? Even five minutes keeps the streak and the forgetting curve at bay.
✨ Mistakes are proof you're trying. Keep collecting them.

service.title: What Studytracker is
items: Studytracker is a web app for studying: materials, notes, questions, dictionaries, reviews and statistics. It is provided by Oleksii Slipokurov (Norway), "we" below.
You need an account to use it. You sign in with an email link or with Google, so keep your email account safe. One account is for one person.
By using Studytracker you agree to these terms and the privacy policy.

plans.title: Plans
items: Free is free for good: everything for studying and monthly AI quotas.
Plus raises the AI quotas for one account. Duo gives the same to two people: each has their own account, materials and quotas.
Room for materials, notes and words doesn't depend on the plan: everyone has the same very high caps, which only protect the service from scripts.
AI quotas count per calendar month and renew on the first day.

payment.title: Payment
items: Paid plans are sold by Stripe through its Link service as the merchant of record. You pay on Stripe's secure page; we never see your card.
Prices include VAT and other taxes, which Stripe works out by where the buyer is. In Norway you pay in kroner, in the US in dollars, elsewhere in your local currency at Stripe's rate.
Link sends receipts and invoices. On your statement the payment shows as LINK.COM* STUDYTRACKER.
If there is a free trial, the payment page shows it, and Link reminds you before it ends.

cancel.title: Renewal and cancelling
items: A subscription renews by itself every month or year until you cancel it.
You can cancel any time: Plan and limits → Manage subscription, or on link.com. The plan lasts to the end of the paid period and nothing more is charged.
After that your account moves to Free. Nothing is deleted or locked; only the AI quotas get smaller.
The same place lets you switch between Plus and Duo, change your card or download invoices.
If a payment fails, Stripe tries again a few times, and the plan keeps working for 7 more days.

refunds.title: Refunds
items: If you are a consumer in Norway, the EU or the EEA, you can withdraw from your first purchase within 14 days. Write to us and we refund the payment. If you already used the plan in those days, the law lets us keep a part for the time used.
Later, the current period is usually not refunded, but cancelling stops all further charges.
Link support also helps with payments and refunds: support.link.com.
These terms don't limit your rights as a consumer under the law.

duo.title: Duo
items: One person, the payer, takes and pays for Duo. They invite one more person with a link that lasts 7 days and works once.
The member has everything in Plus while the payer's Duo is active. If the payer cancels Duo, moves to Plus or stops paying, both go back to Free.
The payer can remove the member, and the member can leave. You see each other's email, and each person's materials stay private.

content.title: Your content
items: Everything you create belongs to you. You let us store and process it only to run the service: for example, to show you a material or send text to an AI feature.
Materials are private until you share a link or publish them in the library. Anyone can see and copy what you publish, and copies stay with people after the material leaves the library.
Only publish what you have the rights to. We may remove a material from the library if it breaks these terms or someone else's rights.
You can download all your data or delete your account on the Account page.

ai.title: AI features
items: AI writes questions, dictionaries and summaries, checks answers and explains mistakes. The text it needs goes to AI providers, listed in the privacy policy.
AI can be wrong, also when the mistake is already in your material or a saved answer. Check what matters, especially before an exam.
AI quotas depend on your plan; failed requests don't count.

rules.title: Rules
items: Don't break the law or other people's rights, publish offensive or harmful content, try to break the service, get around quotas, create content in bulk with scripts or resell access.
If the rules are broken, we may limit features or close the account; where we can, we warn first.

changes.title: Changes
items: We keep developing Studytracker and may change features. We tell you about a new price for a running subscription at least 30 days ahead; it applies from the next period, and you can cancel before then.
We announce important changes to these terms on the site or by email.
If we ever close the service, we tell you in advance and give you time to download your data.

law.title: Liability and law
items: We do our best to keep Studytracker running well, but we can't promise it will never stop or make a mistake.
As far as the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect losses, such as an exam result. This doesn't limit liability the law doesn't let us limit, or your rights as a consumer.
Norwegian law applies. Let's try to settle things directly first; a consumer can also turn to Forbrukerrådet or a court where they live.

contact.title: Contact
items: Questions about these terms, payment or refunds: write to us through the feedback form on the home page.

page.plansTitle: More AI when you need it
page.plansText: Free stays free for good. Paid plans add AI quotas, and Duo shares it all between two people.
page.freeLine: Everything for studying: materials, reviews, statistics

cancel.a: The plan lasts to the end of the paid period, then your account moves to Free. Materials, notes and words stay; only the AI quotas get smaller.

duo.a: The payer invites one more person with a link. Each has their own account, materials and AI quotas, and one person pays.

change.a: Yes, in Manage subscription: between Plus and Duo, and between monthly and yearly. Stripe works out the difference.

currency.q: Which currency, and is tax included?
currency.a: Prices include tax. In Norway you pay in kroner, in the US in dollars, elsewhere in your local currency at Stripe's rate.

refund.q: How do I get a refund?
refund.a: Within 14 days of your first payment, write to us and we refund it. The terms of service have the details.

consent.title: May we count visits?
consent.text: With your permission Google Analytics shows us which pages help and which don't. No ads, no names, no emails, and the site works the same either way.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Studytracker keeps only what it needs to help you learn. Here is what that is, who helps run the site, and how to take your data with you or remove it.

data.title: What we keep
data.text: Your email from signing in; what you create: materials, notes, drawings, questions, dictionaries, attempts and review history; and your settings such as time zone and languages. Nobody else sees your materials unless you share a link or publish to the library.

analytics.title: Visit statistics
analytics.text: Only if you allow it, Google Analytics counts which pages are opened, from what kind of device and roughly from which country. Shared links are sent without their secret part, and nothing that names you is sent. Advertising features are off. You can change your choice at any time with “Cookies” at the bottom of the page.

errors.title: Errors and speed
errors.text: When something breaks, technical details of the error go to Sentry (servers in the EU) so we can fix it. Vercel Speed Insights measures how fast pages load, without cookies and without identifying you.

ai.title: AI features
ai.text: When you use an AI feature, the text it needs (for example a material's content or your answer) is sent to the AI provider for that one request: Anthropic, OpenAI or Google.

services.title: Who helps run the site
services.text: Supabase (sign-in), Microsoft Azure (server and database), Vercel (website), Resend (emails), Sentry (error reports), Google (visit statistics, only with consent), Stripe (payments, only if you buy a plan; we never see card details) and the AI providers above. Voice input uses your browser's speech recognition: to turn speech into text the browser may send the audio to its provider (Google in Chrome). We never receive or store the audio, only the finished text.

rights.title: Your data, your choice
rights.text: On the Account page you can download everything we keep about you or delete your account for good. Reminder emails can be turned off in the statistics page settings.

contact.title: Questions
contact.text: Write to us through the feedback form on the home page.

meta.title: Guide: how to use Studytracker
meta.description: A visual guide to Studytracker: materials, notes, essays with checks, questions, self-defending, flashcards, daily review and how it all works under the hood.

hero.title: Everything about Studytracker,
hero.text: How it all fits together, where to find things and why they work the way they do. The demos are live: tap, switch, try.

add.title: Add a material
add.text: An article, a video, a test or anything you study.

ask.title: Create questions
ask.text: Yourself or with AI, from the text of a material or note.

defend.title: Defend your knowledge
defend.text: Take a self-defending round and see what still cracks.

start.title: A material is the heart of it all
start.lead: Everything you study lives in a material: its text, notes, dictionaries, questions and attempts.
start.how: Press “+” in the materials list, give it a name, pick a type and status. Paste the text yourself or import an article from a link.
start.where: Materials → “+” at the top of the list.
start.why: When everything about one topic sits together, reviewing and testing yourself is far easier.
tips: Give a material a subject: the list is easier to filter and statistics show your weakest subjects.
Search by the name of a material, note or subject; the / key puts the cursor straight into the search.
Fold the list away to give the text more room.

notes.title: Four kinds of notes
notes.lead: Text, drawing, summary and essay, for different ways of thinking.
notes.how: In an open material, press “+” next to “Notes” and pick a type. Everything saves by itself as soon as you pause.
notes.why: What you write in your own words sticks better, and every note can have its own questions.
tips: AI writes the summary from the whole material, its notes and dictionaries; one per material.
Dictate instead of typing: voice input remembers the language you chose.
Paste a screenshot straight into a note with Ctrl/⌘ + V.

essay.title: Essays with an honest check
essay.lead: Write an essay for a task and AI scores it on four criteria from 0 to 100, with specific corrections.
essay.how: Create an “Essay” note, paste the wording of the task, write the text (30 words or more) and press “Check essay”.
essay.why: You see more than a score: exactly what holds it back, be it task response, logic, vocabulary or grammar.
tips: Only the quality of the writing is judged; your opinion never affects the score.
The last result is kept with the essay and is still there after a reload.
Fixed the mistakes? Press “Check again” and compare.

questions.title: Questions that really test you
questions.lead: Three types cover almost everything: open, options (one or several correct) and true/false.
questions.how: Add questions yourself or ask AI to draft some from the text of a material or note, then edit them to suit you.
questions.where: A material or note → the “Questions” tab.
questions.why: Answering from memory does more than re-reading: it is what makes knowledge stick.
tips: Be honest about difficulty: hard questions weigh three times as much.
Add an explanation to a question; it helps when you get it wrong.

defend.title: Self-defending instead of cramming
defend.lead: A quiz from the material's questions: random order, shuffled options and your confidence next to every answer.
defend.how: Press “Start Self Defending”, choose the difficulty and the number of questions, and go.
defend.why: Confidence next to an answer shows where you are wrong even when you feel sure.
tips: After an attempt AI briefly explains every mistake.
Questions you answered unsure come back for review.

score.title: An honest score from 0 to 100
score.lead: Every answer gets a score, and the attempt score is a weighted average where hard questions count more.
score.how: Open answers are first compared word for word, then fuzzily (a typo costs nothing), and AI checks the ones that say the same in other words.
score.where: The results after each attempt, and statistics.
score.why: The score reflects understanding, not perfect spelling.
tips: Options with several correct ones give partial credit for a partly right choice.
Exactly how an answer is checked is shown step by step below, under “Under the hood”.

words.title: Dictionaries and flashcards
words.lead: Words with translation, transcription, article, examples and synonyms, and cards that come back just in time.
words.how: Create a dictionary in a material, add words yourself or with AI and practise them with flashcards.
words.where: A material → a dictionary → the “Flashcards” tab.
words.why: Spaced repetition shows a word right when you are about to forget it.
tips: “Don't know” or “Unsure” opens a mini quiz: the next word comes once you answer it right.
Swipe the cards or press ← ↓ →; space flips the card.

lookup.title: Any word into your dictionary
lookup.lead: Select an unknown word in a material or note and its translation, grammar and an example appear right next to it.
lookup.how: Select a word or phrase, check the suggestion and press “Add to dictionary”. The sentence it came from becomes the example.
lookup.where: Any text of a material or note.
lookup.why: Words learnt from context stay longer than words from a list.
tips: If the word is already in the dictionary, Studytracker says so and won't add it twice.
Translations are in the language set in your profile.

today.title: Daily review
today.lead: One queue a day: the questions and words from all your materials that are due.
today.how: Open “Today”, press “Start” and go through everything that is waiting.
today.where: Navigation → “Today”. The number next to it shows how much is waiting.
today.why: A few minutes a day keep knowledge better than a night before the exam.
tips: Your streak grows when you review every day, and freezes save a missed day.
Email reminders are set up in your account.

deadlines.title: Deadlines and calendar
deadlines.lead: Give a material the date of an exam or a hand-in and see how much time is left.
deadlines.how: Set a deadline in the material; the calendar shows it together with the days you studied.
deadlines.why: With the date in sight, reviews are easier to spread out instead of squeezing them into the last evening.
tips: A few days before the exam, run self-defending with only the hard questions.

statistics.title: Statistics that give you hints
statistics.lead: Score trend, streak, accuracy by difficulty, confidence calibration and your weakest subjects.
statistics.how: Just learn: statistics gather themselves from every attempt and review.
statistics.why: You see not only how much you studied but what to work on next.
tips: “Focus areas” lists the subjects with the lowest accuracy; start with those.

library.title: A library of ready materials
library.lead: Languages, programming and more: materials with questions and dictionaries that you can add in one click.
library.how: Open the library, look through a material and add it: you get your own copy.
library.where: Navigation → “Library”. It is open even without signing in.
library.why: No need to start from scratch: take something ready and practise right away.
tips: You can also propose your own material for the library.

share.title: Share and learn together
share.lead: A link gives a friend a full copy of a material: notes, dictionaries and questions. Your attempts and progress stay yours.
share.how: In a material, press “Share” and copy the link.
share.why: Learning as a pair is more fun, and on the Duo plan each of you has your own AI quotas.
tips: Changes in someone else's copy never touch yours.

ai.title: AI that helps, not decides
ai.lead: Questions from text, answers checked by meaning, mistakes explained, summaries, words and essays, whenever you press the button.
ai.how: Look for buttons with a sparkle ✨: next to them you see how many requests are left this month.
ai.where: Questions, dictionaries, summaries, essays and attempt results.
ai.why: AI takes the routine, the thinking stays yours.
tips: Limits renew on the first day of every month, and failed requests are not counted.
You can choose the language of AI explanations in your profile.

hood.title: How it all works inside
hood.text: No magic: here is what happens to your answer, your memory and your data.

score.title: From an answer to a score
score.text: An open answer goes through several checks and stops at the first one that gives a sure result.
score.question: Question:

exact.title: Exact match
exact.text: Word for word, ignoring case and spaces.

ai.title: AI by meaning
ai.text: Only for the “grey zone”: close, but in other words.

score.title: Score
score.text: From 0 to 100, then into the attempt score.

examples.exact: Word for word: 100 straight away and nothing else is checked.
examples.typo: One typo: the fuzzy match recognises the word and the score is nearly full.
examples.meaning: Other words, same meaning: the answer is in the grey zone, so AI judges the meaning itself.
examples.wrong: Not it at all: a score of 0, AI isn't even asked, and the question comes back for review.

memory.title: Reviews at the right moment
memory.text: The FSRS algorithm tracks how fast you forget each word and question and schedules a review when your chance of recalling it drops to about 90%. The better you know it, the less often you see it.
memory.chart: A forgetting curve that falls more slowly after every review
memory.caption: Every review makes the curve flatter, so the gaps grow: days, a week, several weeks. The 90% goal can be changed in your learning settings.

ai.title: AI only when you ask
ai.text: Text goes to AI only when you press the button, and only what that task needs.

quota.title: Fair limits
quota.text: AI requests are counted per month and failed ones are not taken off. How many are left shows next to every button.

autosave.title: Autosave
autosave.text: Notes, essays and drawings save themselves as soon as you pause.

export.title: Export any time
export.text: Download all your data from your account: a ZIP with JSON and a word table for Anki.

tips.title: Small things that save time
tips.text: Keys and tricks worth knowing from day one.

search.title: Quick search
search.text: In the materials list press / and search by name, note or subject.

flashcards.title: Flashcards from the keyboard
flashcards.text: ← don't know, ↓ unsure, → know; space flips the card.

links.title: Links in notes
links.text: Hold Ctrl or ⌘ and click a link to open it in a new tab.

paste.title: Images from the clipboard
paste.text: Copy a screenshot and paste it straight into a note.

voice.title: Voice input
voice.text: Dictate notes and answers; the recognition language you pick is remembered.

select.title: A word into the dictionary
select.text: Select a word in a material or note and a translation appears next to it with an “Add” button.

install.title: Like an app
install.text: Install Studytracker from your browser's menu and it opens in its own window like any other app.

theme.title: Theme and language
theme.text: Light or dark theme and the interface language switch at the top of the page.

free.a: Yes, the Free plan costs nothing. AI features have monthly limits, and Plus and Duo give more AI requests and more room for materials.

private.a: Only you. You can share with a link that gives a separate copy, or propose a material for the library.

quota.q: What if my AI limit runs out?
quota.a: Everything else works as usual: notes, questions, self-defending, flashcards. Limits renew on the first of the month, and the “Limits” page shows how many are left.

export.q: How do I take my data with me?
export.a: Your account has an export: a ZIP with all your materials, notes, questions and dictionaries, plus a word table for Anki.

languages.a: The interface is in Ukrainian, English and Norwegian. AI explanations come in any of 11 languages, and you can learn anything.
